papers.name: A Skeleton-based View-Invariant Framework for Human Fall Detection in an Elevator
papers.headline: Fall detection across camera viewpoints.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Elevator cameras see people from different angles, while emergency fall examples are difficult to collect.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The published framework combines AlphaPose 2D keypoints, 3D pose estimation, Procrustes alignment to a reference camera, and a fall-recognition model.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Co-authored with Rashid Ali, Lan-Da Van, and Yu-Chee Tseng. The related public thesis repository contains my pose-conversion, tuning, and visualization work.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Published at ICIT 2022. The work studies transferring recognition across camera views; the case study does not claim a deployed safety certification.

metadata.label: Publication
metadata.value: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Technology (ICIT)

papers.name: A Smart Door Prototype with a Face Recognition Capability
papers.headline: Computer vision meets a physical door.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Explore touch-free access by connecting face recognition to a physical door-lock prototype.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The paper describes a Raspberry Pi 3B, servo actuator, Python, Node-RED, Blynk, MQTT, Haar-cascade detection, LBPH recognition, and Google Assistant integration.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Co-authored with Handy Wicaksono. My smart-door project connects the software, recognition workflow, and physical demonstration.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Published in IJRA 11(1), pages 1-9. The original demonstration lets visitors inspect the prototype; it is a research system, not a commercial security guarantee.

metadata.label: Publication
metadata.value: IAES International Journal of Robotics and Automation 11(1), 1-9

papers.name: Integration of Smart Door Lock with Face Recognition based on Raspberry Pi 3 with Google Assistant Features
papers.headline: A connected door, controlled through recognition and voice.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Bring camera-based recognition and voice interaction into a Raspberry Pi smart-door prototype.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The publication connects face recognition, Raspberry Pi 3, and Google Assistant. The related prototype demonstrates the interaction with a physical door.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: This earlier smart-door publication is part of my embedded-systems research. The linked record preserves the original publication credit.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Retained as an earlier publication, distinct from the later IJRA paper. The original record was not fully readable during this review, so additional experimental claims are omitted.

papers.name: Towards Integration of Heterogeneous Controllers in an IOT-based Automation System
papers.headline: Different controllers, one connected automation workflow.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Automation installations combine PLCs and microcontrollers that do not naturally share one communication interface.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The research uses Node-RED to connect heterogeneous devices and services. The published cases include an elderly smart-home prototype, a recognition-based smart door, and separated-house automation.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Co-authored with Handy Wicaksono, Petrus Santoso, Iwan Handoyo Putro, and Pricilia Alvina. This was collaborative connected-systems research.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Published in E3S Web of Conferences 188, article 00009. The research demonstrates device integration and information flow rather than claiming a deployed industrial platform.

papers.name: Understanding Engineering Students’ Behaviours when Writing Group Report using Wiki
papers.headline: Understanding the human side of collaborative tools.

story.title: The problem
story.text: A shared group report can conceal uneven contribution and difficult group dynamics.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The study follows engineering students writing laboratory reports with Wiki, using questionnaires, observations, and logbooks to examine participation.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Co-authored with Iwan Handoyo Putro, Petrus Santoso, Handry Khoswanto, and Handy Wicaksono. The publication is a team research contribution.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Published in E3S Web of Conferences 188, article 00014. Findings emphasize preparation, monitoring, and feedback in collaborative learning; they are not an AI-model result.

patents.name: AI-based Abnormal Behavior Detection System for Elevators
patents.headline: Detecting abnormal passenger behavior across different elevator camera viewpoints.

story.title: The problem
story.text: A behavior detector must handle different viewpoints inside an elevator car.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The published method extracts 2D body features, reconstructs a 3D reference, transforms the viewpoint, projects to 2D, and applies behavior detection.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Listed as a co-inventor within the research team. This describes the public invention at a high level; patent ownership remains with the recorded assignee.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Taiwan patent I893176, granted August 11, 2025. The public record describes the invention; no unverified deployment or performance metric is added.

patents.name: Energy-efficient Abnormal Passenger Behavior Detection Method and Elevator System
patents.headline: An energy-efficient approach to detecting abnormal passenger behavior inside elevators.

story.title: The problem
story.text: Elevator passenger-behavior detection also needs to consider energy use during operation.

story.title: The approach
story.text: The granted invention concerns an elevator system and an energy-efficient passenger-behavior detection method. Only its publicly documented scope is summarized here.

story.title: My contribution
story.text: Listed as a co-inventor within the research team. The certificate and the laboratory publication record provide the public attribution.

story.title: The outcome
story.text: Taiwan patent I883252, granted May 11, 2025. The public certificate confirms the grant; it does not establish a measured energy-saving result.
